items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: And that’s where the first proper like modern jazz group that me and Andrew Dickenson who is a drummer who teaches at Sydney Conservatorium.

ctx.x: Yeah. There are so many things that happen to young musicians along the way up and I think busking and, you know I was reading your bios and things on your website and it sounds like you were in and out of a number of bands, and there’s a lot of education that goes on in that.

Yeah. I met some musicians — I was 17 at the jazz camp. I went to a classical camp, found out about a jazz camp, so the next school holiday I went to that jazz camp. And that’s where the first proper like modern jazz group that me and Andrew Dickenson who is a drummer who teaches at Sydney Conservatorium. All of us are still playing. It was Adrian Mears on trombone, who is based in Europe; Nicki on bass; and John Foreman on piano, who actually in the “Idol” of Australia he’s done things like “Australian Idol” and…
Do you recall what you got paid the first time you did a paying gig?
